ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. If $\angle DOC = 110^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DAC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Given rectangle ABCD,\\
hence DO=AO,\\
thus $\angle$ADO=$\angle$DAO,\\
since $\angle$DOC=110$^\circ$,\\
thus 2$\angle$DAO=110$^\circ$, i.e., $\angle$DAO=55$^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$DAC=\boxed{55^\circ}.

method.method_draft: Use the intersecting diagonals to form triangle AOD. From the image, read that A is bottom-left, D is top-left, C is top-right, B is bottom-right, and O is the intersection of diagonals AC and BD, so A, O, C are collinear and D, O, B are collinear. From the text, use that ABCD is a rectangle and ∠DOC = 110°. In a rectangle, diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so AO is half of AC and DO is half of BD; since AC = BD, AO = DO. Thus triangle AOD is isosceles, giving ∠DAO = ∠ADO. Because OC is the extension of OA, ∠DOC is an exterior angle of triangle AOD at O, so ∠DOC = ∠DAO + ∠ADO = 2∠DAO. Therefore ∠DAO = 55°. Since O lies on AC, ∠DAO = ∠DAC, so ∠DAC = 55°.

From the image, read that AC rises from A to C and BD falls from D to B, crossing at O inside the rectangle; AD is vertical and AB, DC are horizontal. From the text, use that ABCD is a rectangle and ∠DOC = 110°. Let θ be the angle that diagonal AC makes with the horizontal side AB.
